subject: Art & Design
title: Biophilic Design: Buildings That Love Nature
description: Learn Biophilic Design: Buildings That Love Nature in one minute.

hook.text: Offices with natural light, plants, and water features reduce sick days by 15%. Buildings affect health.

buildup.text: Biophilic design integrates nature into built environments: daylight, greenery, natural materials, and organic shapes.

discovery.text: Humans evolved in nature. Our brains still respond to natural patterns with reduced stress and improved focus.

twist.text: Singapore's Jewel Changi Airport has a 40-meter indoor waterfall surrounded by a forest.

climax.text: Amazon's Seattle HQ includes giant glass spheres filled with 40,000 plants. Workers meet among trees.

punchline.text: The future of architecture isn't escaping nature. It's inviting it back in.

quiz.question: Why does biophilic design improve occupant well-being?
options: Human brains evolved in nature and respond to natural elements with reduced stress
Plants release chemicals that make people more productive
Natural materials are cheaper than synthetic ones

details.summary: Biophilic design integrates natural elements — daylight, plants, water, natural materials, and views of nature — into built environments. Research shows it reduces stress, improves productivity, and accelerates healing.
details.whyItMatters: Humans evolved in nature and our biology responds to natural stimuli. Biophilic design applies this science to architecture, creating buildings that measurably improve occupant health, wellbeing, and cognitive performance.
takeaways: Integrates daylight, plants, water, and natural materials
Research shows reduced stress and improved productivity
Amazon's Spheres and Jewel Changi are landmark examples

faq.question: What evidence supports biophilic design?
faq.answer: Studies show hospital patients with nature views heal faster. Office workers with daylight and plants report 15% higher wellbeing. Schools with natural ventilation and views improve test scores. The evidence base spans healthcare, workplace productivity, and educational performance.

faq.question: Is biophilic design just adding plants to buildings?
faq.answer: Plants are one element, but true biophilic design is holistic — natural light patterns, water features, natural materials, prospect and refuge spaces, and visual connections to outdoor landscapes. It's about recreating the sensory richness of natural environments, not decoration.
